There are many videos on youtube showing it on a variety of screens. But basically, if you brought a magnet to a color CRT, it would magnetize the grill on the front and make the electron beam lose alignment, so it missed the intended subpixels, you would get a rainbowy pattern of color distortion, and in worse cases actual distortion on the image itself as well.

A degausser is basically a device that will produce an oscillating magnetic field to scramble and neutralize magnetization; some were standalone devices, but as time passed, screens started having them built-in. When activated, they would produce a quickly oscillating magnetic field of decreasing strength, making a *tweng* sound as it went, at first the rainbowy pattern gets worse, much more bands and much more complex pattern, moving across the screen, and the image vibrates and waves, then as the power goes down the size of the bands grow and eventually they're so big they're bigger than the screen and all the colors are right once again and the image undistorted; often at the end of the procedure you hear a click sound as the circuit is turned off.
I'm 25. I sat there for a moment until it hit me. That was pretty sweet.
